messages:
Anya: Ran a perfetto + nsys capture on the night regression run. Observed a ~250ms tail spike on the request path at ~00:02:14 that aligns with a burst of Triton-like compile events. Link to perfetto slice: https://perfetto.local/trace/0xdeadbeef (private). Attached nsys .qdrep.
Sam: Looking at the capture — I can see three consecutive compile windows (~60-90ms each) and repeated cudaLaunchKernel spikes immediately after. Kernel-cache shows repeated misses for the same logical op signature.
Ravi: Can you paste the timeline snippet where the compiles happen? Also what's the batching config for that run? My hunch: a heterogeneous batch ended up selecting different kernel variants, invalidating cache entries.
Anya: Timeline excerpt copied from perfetto flame:
```
[00:02:12] nvtx: batch_build start
[00:02:13] triton.compile (model_kernel_A) 85ms
[00:02:13] cudaLaunchKernel (matmul_v2_quant) 7ms
[00:02:13] triton.compile (model_kernel_A_alt) 72ms
[00:02:14] cudaLaunchKernel (matmul_v2_fp) 10ms
[00:02:14] triton.compile (model_kernel_A) 88ms
```
Config: batcher: max_batch=8, strategy=latency_favor, kv_cache_enabled=true, kv_prefetch=false. Workload: many short and medium sequences, mix of quantized ops.
Benchbot: [perf-alert] p99 latency +18% on mainline after deploy 1792290000. Tagged eng-runtime.
Lee: Note — I merged the quant-matmul-ordering PR yesterday that flips the kernel preference to prefer quantized variant when qcoverage > 0.1. That could change which kernel is chosen first (and thus cache behavior).
Sam: If preference order changed without adding it to the cache key, we can get cache churn. Quick checklist:
  1) instrument kernel_cache.lookup to log key components (model, shape, seq_len_bucket, prefer_quantized, kv_primed)
  2) add NVTX markers around compile paths in the runtime
  3) run synthetic batcher with --batch-sim=hetero to reproduce
Ravi: Proposed quick patch to kernel cache key (pseudo):
```
def build_cache_key(op, shape, config):
    return f"{op}:{shape}:{config.seq_bucket}:{int(config.prefer_quantized)}:{int(config.kv_primed)}"

# also bump warm eviction to 10m while warmup flag is true
```
Adding prefer_quantized and kv_primed should stop identical ops from being treated as different when preference flips.
Anya: Running a repro now with the synthetic harness. Command:
```
python infra/perf/run_workload.py --model=redwood-7b --mode=warmup-heavy \
  --batcher=max:8 --strategy=latency_favor --trace=nvtx --nsys-capture
```
I'll attach new nsys once done and post kernel_cache stats.
Lee: If this reproduces, we should roll back the quant order change or make kernel preference an explicit opt-in flag for canary. Short-term: pin old order in Dedicated and route canary traffic selectively.
Sam: Short mitigation idea: if the batcher sees >N distinct signature candidates in a single aggregation window, switch that batch to "per-request" scheduling (avoid building a mega-batch that forces multiple compiles). N could be 2 or 3.
Anya: Got it. Running now; will report back in this thread with nsys link + kernel_cache logs. Thanks all.:thumbsup:
__note: This is a single Slack thread string; messages are in chronological order and prefixed by sender name.
